answer: Identity bonds that decay keep fakes out of the harbor market. Each agent locks a 200-coin bond that loses 5% every epoch unless renewed by real work, like timber that rots when never used. An honest agent pays once, renews through real jobs, and keeps undiluted rewards. Forging 1000 identities costs 1000 x 200 = 200,000 coins, and idle bonds keep shrinking, so fakes must keep topping up or vanish. A whisper from peers flags idle bonds for audit.
